hook.text: Warehouses full of spare parts cost companies billions.

buildup.text: A digital inventory replaces physical shelves. When a part is needed, a local printer produces it in hours, not weeks.

discovery.text: The US military prints parts on aircraft carriers and forward bases, cutting resupply wait from months to days.

twist.text: Parts for vintage cars, old appliances, and discontinued products can be reverse-engineered and printed from 3D scans.

climax.text: Deutsche Bahn prints over 100 different spare parts for trains that original manufacturers no longer produce.

punchline.text: If the part is obsolete, print it. If the warehouse is empty, print it.

quiz.question: How does Deutsche Bahn use 3D printing for its trains?
options: Prints spare parts no longer manufactured
